title: Grateful Dead Live at Golden Hall Community Concourse on 1970-08-05
lineage: SBD > MR > Reel > PCM > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality acoustic set with rare mandolin‑flavored gems (El Paso, Ballad of Casey Jones) captured from a soundboard source that suffers from hiss and a muddy mix.
ai_review.review: The show is an intimate early‑70s acoustic affair highlighted by rare numbers such as “Drink Up And Go Home,” “A Voice From On High,” and a superb rendition of “El Paso.” Reviewers rave about the relaxed, almost gospel‑like vibe and the mandolin work (David Nelson or possibly Jerry) but note that the tape is noisy, with hiss, muddy balance and vocals that sit low in the mix.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈70 %) award 4‑5 stars and praise the performance, while technical complaints are consistent but not dominant, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss and a muddy mix are repeatedly mentioned; mandolin sits too high in the left channel, vocals are low on several tracks, and drums are described as over‑busy. Some reviewers still call the sound “excellent” or “very nice” despite these issues.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is laid‑back and gospel‑tinged, with a relaxed acoustic flow that feels like a small‑room worship service. Rare tunes are interspersed with familiar folk/country numbers, creating an almost “church‑like” experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his guitar tone (e.g., on “Lay Me Down”) and the mysterious mandolin work – some reviewers think he’s playing mandolin; others note David Nelson may be the mandolinist.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned as providing a restrained but solid bass foundation that adds mass to the acoustic setting.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mixed opinions: Mickey is credited by some, while Bill Kreutzmann is called out for being too busy or “jazzed out.” One reviewer calls the drum track in the right channel “lame.”
